rows.issue: The single-dimple map is not the record
rows.detail: By 015b's map, the dimples a dome-class build holds (1-5 mm) imply gamma 0.69-0.90, and a reflector-class build (0.15 mm) about 0.95. The only measured large sandwich domes, S-II's, were built with a 0.254 mm core-to-face fit and inflation-faired skins, and reached about 0.21-0.22 (035, CHECK-035). The map transfers to a sandwich at Vc 0.95 only through t_eq (015b NFI-015B-SANDWICH).
rows.to_close: A built sandwich shell with measured shape and measured knockdown: 038 T7, or a subscale shell built by this route.

rows.issue: S-II's shape and specimens are unpublished in the sources opened
rows.detail: No as-built contour RMS or peak exists for the S-II or S-IVB bulkheads. The CR-1457 hemisphere specimen details (SDL 468) are unread.
rows.to_close: Retrieve SDL 468 and S-II acceptance records.

rows.detail: SR-200 at 0.795 mm is in the 0.020-0.058 in class sold 'at narrower widths and shorter lengths' than 24 x 72 in (DS-HPP-613). The 028b blank of 0.6096 x 1.8288 m is a projection; smaller sheets multiply blanks and seams (020: up to 6,764 per skin).

rows.issue: Doubly curved Be forming at blank size is unmeasured
rows.detail: Solar's 0.003 in conformance was on a cylindrical 1 x 2 ft panel (10 ft radius). Lockheed's 39 in skins warped from thermal gradients, and it advised forming square sections and splicing. No doubly curved Be blank near 0.6 x 1.8 m has a measured contour.
rows.to_close: Forming trial on one full blank (F1).

rows.issue: Forming residual stress is this card's estimate
rows.detail: Conforming a flat blank elastically to R 10 m takes about 4.6e-4 strain across a 0.61 m width (67 MPa) and about 1.2e-3 over the half-diagonal disc, which is at Be's elastic limit. CSO saw 150 um panel rebound from the same effect in 1.0 mm Al.
rows.to_close: Measure residual stress and springback on F1.

rows.issue: The face-core cure is set by 037b
rows.detail: 037b (filed 03:24) finds the continuous core bond survives once the faces carry the in-plane load. A bond stress-free above 54 C instead loads 028b's 30:1 scarf: at 250 F, 4.4 MPa takes usage from 0.972 to 1.052. Its lightest fix, adopted here, is AF 163-2U's 200 F cure plus a 30.34:1 scarf (+0.12 kg). Free core edges read 1.08-1.51 at 200 F. A room-temperature paste would cost 25.1 kg per 10 g/m2 on both bond lines (this card).
rows.to_close: 037b's checker (ord-admiral-rr2-check037b-codex-7e53-1020), then a bonded witness at 200 F.

rows.issue: Seams must cure in place at room temperature
rows.detail: A strip 100 K hotter than the cold shell carries about 354 MPa (this card), above 345 MPa, so heat-blanket cure is excluded on the shell. No room-temperature 30:1 scarf data in Be exist. EA 9394 and EA 9309.3NA give 29-33 MPa lap shear on aluminium (sub-worker rows).
rows.to_close: Room-temperature scarf witnesses in SR-200 (038 T2 extended).

rows.issue: No inspection method for scarf seams
rows.detail: No source inspects a 30:1 bonded scarf. E2580 UT assumes parallel surfaces, and shearography needs two shear directions on strip debonds.
rows.to_close: Develop and validate a seam NDE on witness strips.

rows.issue: Bond NDE for Be on Al honeycomb is unproven
rows.detail: Tap-test a90/95 is 28-43 mm on 0.5 mm Al skins, about the 29-55 mm disbond that buckles the inner face at 300 MPa (this card). Flash thermography likely cannot see the far bond under conductive Be (inference). Weak and kissing bonds escape commercial NDE.
rows.to_close: PoD study on Be-faced panels with seeded disbonds.

rows.issue: Holding shape through closure is a projection
rows.detail: There is no precedent for a 20 m thin-metal sandwich sphere. Large spheres held +/-6 mm (SNO 12 m) to under 2 cm (Moss R 18.3 m), which is global and cm-class. The S-II inflation technique smoothed welded skins to fit the core; using an inflated inner skin as the mandrel is this card's proposal.
rows.to_close: Subscale assembly trial of either method.

rows.issue: Be dust limits where scarfs are cut
rows.detail: OSHA 1910.1024 sets a PEL of 0.2 ug/m3, so scarfing and trimming Be is regulated-area work (sub-worker row). JPL had all dust-producing Be operations done at the supplier. The route puts every Be cut before assembly.

rows.issue: Be face waviness at the wrinkle wavelength is unmeasured
rows.detail: The precedents are whole-panel RMS (reflectors 5-60 um; vendor honeycomb 0.2 mm) or cell depths. Treated as wrinkle-band amplitude, they map to Q 0.19-0.75 (this card). Wrinkle periods are near 37-40 mm (CHECK-032).
rows.to_close: Profilometry of a bonded Be/CR-III panel in the 20-60 mm band (F1, 038 T3).

rows.issue: Jig support spacing is this card's estimate
rows.detail: Self-weight is 34.2 Pa. A sandwich span sags 0.11 mm at 2 m and 4.2 mm at 5 m (simply supported strip), so supports belong 2 m apart or closer.

rows.issue: The first evacuation is the proof, and it is destructive
rows.detail: Sea-level evacuation loads the hull to 1.061 of its 500 m design pressure (038). A buckle at proof ends the hull, and no subscale proof precedes it.
rows.to_close: A subscale built shell evacuated first (T7).

rows.detail: Reflector-grade surfaces cost GBP 2-5M to refurbish or replace a 15 m dish (JCMT, 2011 talk) and about $5-6M per 10 m SMT (1987). Nothing here scales that to a 20 m sphere. Be stock is 020's $39.5-167.9M.
The route adopts 037b's 200 F panel cure and 30.34:1 scarf. If CHECK-037b moves the stress-free temperature or the scarf rule, step 4 and the seam overlap change.
rows.to_close: Re-read step 4 against CHECK-037b when it files.
